\begin{proof}
Let $G$ be a group of order $462=2\cdot3\cdot7\cdot11=11\cdot42$. By Sylow's theorems, the number $n_{11}$ of Sylow $11$-subgroups satisfies
\[
n_{11}\equiv 1\pmod{11}\qquad\text{and}\qquad n_{11}\mid 42.
\]
The positive divisors of $42$ are $1,2,3,6,7,14,21,42$, and the only one congruent to $1$ modulo $11$ is $1$. Thus $n_{11}=1$. Therefore the unique Sylow $11$-subgroup is normal in $G$. It has order $11$, so it is a nontrivial proper normal subgroup of $G$. Hence $G$ is not simple.
\end{proof}
